bull_bear.body:
- Differentiated quality of bone gelatin: despite surplus Chinese supply and cheaper hide-based gelatin, 'the Company has successfully differentiated itself on the quality of bone gelatin, which has maintained its market share'.
- Strength in brand-conscious / regulated customer segments, where demand remained strong and the Company increased market share and ran gelatin capacities at full utilisation, after consciously declining low-quality-conscious Chinese-gelatin customers.
- Raw material sourcing advantage: softening international crushed bone prices let the Company import substantial quantities of Gelbone (premium crushed bone), reducing dependency on domestic raw material with a cost advantage and better yield/quality.
- Access to the overseas promoter Nitta Gelatin Inc., Japan for expertise and market insights in servicing customers to global NITTA Group standards, backed by 100+ years of group collagen expertise.
- Market and channel flexibility: when US tariffs made gelatin uncompetitive in the US, volumes were shifted to the domestic soft-capsule market and to emerging markets without value loss, and tariffs were in several cases passed on to customers.
- Operating discipline: gelatin plant run at full capacity and the collagen peptide plant taken to almost full capacity, with specific power and fuel consumption lower on economies of scale and cost reduction measures.
- Consumer brand build-out with Gelixer, marketed as India's No.1 / first collagen brand with a clinically proven Japanese formula.
- Migration from SAP ECC to SAP S/4 HANA giving advanced workflows, robust controls, MRP-based planning and faster in-memory data processing.
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- US tariff exposure and trade-policy volatility — Management states that with the imposition of US tariffs 'your product Gelatin became uncompetitive in the US market for a substantial period of time', forcing a deliberate reduction of US exposure and redirection of volumes; gelatin exports fell year on year as customers became 'wary about the risk of non-supply, if contracted'. The Chairman's message warns that the potential continuation or expansion of tariff measures by major economies, including the United States, warrants continued caution, and the cautionary statement lists tariffs imposed by the US administration as a factor that may affect operations.
- Raw material cost and supply volatility, concentrated on a single input (crushed bone) — Listed by management as 'Supply Chain Volatility: Fluctuating raw material costs, particularly in the bovine sector, can cause margin pressure.' Crushed bone is described as 'the major raw material of the Company'; FY26 benefited from softened international crushed bone prices and cheaper hydrochloric acid and lime, but the report also notes that 'certain factors have exerted significant pressure on bone gelatin costs'. Mitigation cited is investment in sustainable and traceable sourcing, long-term contracts and development of new cost-effective vendors.
- Substitution by non-animal capsule materials — 'Pressure from substitutes: The growth of plant-based and synthetic (HPMC, Starch) capsules is challenging gelatin in specific, mostly premium or niche markets.' Demand for non-animal-based capsules such as HPMC and Pullulan is said to be increasing rapidly on dietary preferences. Management argues the shift is currently slowed by pharma-grade HPMC's high cost and 16-20-week lead times, and that gelatin remains dominant in the mainstream high-volume pharmaceutical segment - so the risk is structural but paced.
- Competitive displacement by surplus hide-based gelatin and Chinese supply — Surplus Chinese capacity and increased production of bovine hide gelatin and collagen peptides - driven by a weakening leather industry pushing hide suppliers into these outlets, and by closures of bone gelatin plants in the UK and US releasing additional bone - have created surplus supply and weakened bone gelatin demand among low-quality-conscious customers. Capsule makers are increasingly blending hide gelatin with bone gelatin to manage cost.
- Deliberate market-share loss in the price-led segment — 'The Company has taken a conscious call not to service Chinese Gelatin customers due to gap in quality expectation and pricing pressure, which has resulted in a decline in market share in this specific segment.' The strategy concentrates the business in brand-conscious and regulated segments, which held up in FY26 but narrows the addressable base if quality premiums compress.
- Export and geographic concentration — Structural concentration disclosed in the Directors' Report: 'The entire sale of Ossein/Limed Ossein, 33% of the total sale of Gelatin and 69% of Collagen Peptide was through exports.' Ossein/limed ossein is entirely export-dependent and collagen peptide growth in FY26 leaned on a significant increase in North American demand - the same geography exposed to tariff action.
- Price and mix realisation pressure — Prices of Limed Ossein, Gelatin and Bovine Peptide dropped by 9%, 3% and 9% respectively during 2025-26, and while collagen peptide volumes rose 57% the average realisation per unit declined 14.5% because of change in mix - volume growth is not translating one-for-one into value. Management notes price negotiations with both suppliers and customers are carried out on a regular basis to protect margins.
- Regulatory, currency and macro-policy exposure — The cautionary statement enumerates that operations may be affected by the supply and demand situation, tariffs imposed by the US administration, input price and availability, changes in Government Regulations, Tax Laws and foreign exchange rate fluctuations. The report also shows regulation moving both ways for the Company - a new acid regulation made domestic Rock DCP production unviable, which lifted the Company's DCP realisation.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: The Company manufactures gelatin, ossein/limed ossein and collagen peptides from crushed bone, with di-calcium phosphate (DCP) as a by-product, primarily serving pharmaceutical and nutraceutical customers who use hard and soft gelatin capsules as an oral dosage form. It operates three divisions in India (Ossein Division at Kathikudam, Gelatin Division at Kakkanad and the Reva Division in Gujarat) and works with its overseas promoter Nitta Gelatin Inc., Japan to leverage the NITTA Group's technology, quality standards and market insights. During the year it also built out a consumer-facing collagen nutrition brand, Gelixer, positioned as India's first collagen brand.

- **Gelatin:** Bone gelatin for hard gelatin capsules, Bone gelatin for soft gelatin (softgel) capsules
- **Ossein:** Ossein, Limed Ossein
- **Collagen Peptide:** Collagen peptides, Gelixer (consumer collagen nutrition brand), Gelixer CollagenPep (Type I & III bovine collagen peptides), Fish Peptide
- **By-products:** Di-Calcium Phosphate (DCP)

outlook.body:
- Diversify markets and customer base to absorb US tariff disruption: exposure to the US market was deliberately reduced and gelatin volumes shifted to the domestic soft-capsule market and to emerging markets, with tariffs passed on to customers in several cases; the Company looks to bounce back in the US aided by an India-US Free Trade Agreement.
- Grow through capacity expansion in Gelatin and Collagen Peptides - listed explicitly as the 'Economic Sustainability' pillar alongside cost optimisation and supply chain efficiency.
- Compete on quality rather than price in gelatin: a conscious decision NOT to service Chinese-gelatin customers because of the gap in quality expectation and pricing pressure, accepting market-share loss in the low-quality-conscious segment while gaining share in brand-conscious / regulated segments.
- Secure and diversify raw material: invest in sustainable and traceable sourcing and long-term contracts, collaborate with industry participants to develop hide-based raw materials, import Gelbone when international crushed bone prices soften, and develop cost-effective new vendors and sources expected to aid profitability in the coming years.
- Widen the collagen peptide franchise by venturing into new markets and segments outside India, and build the consumer-facing Gelixer collagen nutrition brand (CollagenPep, Collagen Beauty, Collagen Active) positioned as India's first collagen brand.
- Sustained cost competitiveness and operational excellence: streamline operations, reduce costs and maximise output, run employee campaigns for innovative cost-reduction ideas, and hold plant utilisation at full/near-full capacity by rearranging customer and product mix.
- Energy and digital investment: install captive solar plants in two divisions (1.18 MW Gelatin Division, 0.78 MW Ossein Division) and complete the migration from SAP ECC to SAP S/4 HANA, with a proposed warehouse management module using bar coding and hand-held devices for real-time material tracking.
- Leverage the overseas promoter Nitta Gelatin Inc., Japan for technology, quality standards and market insight, and contribute to the Nitta Gelatin Group's Long-Term Management Vision announced in November 2025.
- Position products within a circular-economy / clean-label sustainability narrative: gelatin and collagen peptides are made from by-products of the meat and farmed fish industries, are natural proteins free from preservatives and additives, and sustainability considerations are embedded from product innovation and market development through to capital investments and daily operations.
- Organisation development: leadership continuity and succession (COO inducted, new CFO appointed with the incumbent moving to Chief Risk Officer), a three-tier L&D framework, values embedded into Level 1 leadership KRAs, the TEAM EXCITE engagement platform and an integrated HRMS.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Two named projects dominate the FY2025-26 expansion narrative. First, the Collagen Peptide expansion: the 550 Metric Ton expansion project was completed and commissioned in the second quarter of FY2025-26 and commercial production from the new plant commenced in the same quarter; the Chairman/MD message describes the new Collagen Peptide Project as commissioned with an installed capacity of 3.5 metric tonnes per day. The added capacity fed through to results - the Directors' Report attributes part of the year's performance to 'turnover from the expanded capacity of the Collagen Peptide project', collagen peptide export sales roughly doubled year on year 'aided by capacity additions implemented during the course of the year', and the Company took the Collagen Peptide plant to almost full capacity production during the fiscal year by finding new markets and customers outside India. Second, the ongoing Gelatin Expansion Project is stated to be progressing as per schedule and is expected to enhance manufacturing capabilities and let the Company tap growing gelatin demand from hard/soft capsule delivery formats in pharmaceuticals and nutraceuticals; no completion date, capacity number or rupee quantum is disclosed for it in this bundle. Alongside, captive solar plant installation projects are in progress in two divisions - 1.18 MW for the Gelatin Division and 0.78 MW for the Ossein Division - and the Company has migrated from SAP ECC to SAP S/4 HANA with a proposed warehouse management module using bar coding and hand-held devices. The gelatin plant itself ran at full capacity during 2025-26 by rearranging customer and product mix. Under its Economic Sustainability pillar the Company states a continuing focus on growth initiatives 'including capacity expansion in Gelatin and Collagen Peptides'. No rupee capital-expenditure quantum is disclosed anywhere in this bundle.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- The global capsule market including India is expanding steadily on rising pharmaceutical and nutraceutical reliance on capsules, with gelatin capsules expected to maintain a dominant 85% global market share.
- Near-term outlook for bone gelatin in both hard and soft capsule applications remains positive, supported by rising pharmaceutical production, increasing nutraceutical consumption and technological advances in capsule manufacturing.
- Bovine-derived bone gelatin retains a strong preferred position in pharmaceutical applications on consistent quality, high bloom strength and well-established safety standards, despite alternative materials emerging.
- Nutraceutical expansion is a key driver, with a projected 32% increase in demand for gelatin-based supplements; softgel applications are a 'high value-added segment' and hard gelatin capsules a 'structural demand pillar'.
- Substitution risk is contained near term: while HPMC is growing, its high cost and 16-20-week lead times for pharma-grade material restrict a rapid shift away from gelatin, preserving gelatin's market share in the mainstream high-volume pharmaceutical segment.
- Regional mix: Asia-Pacific is expected to be the fastest-growing region on expanding pharmaceutical manufacturing, while Europe continues to lead demand, particularly for premium and traceable gelatin.
- Collagen peptide demand is structurally supported by preventive healthcare, an ageing population seeking joint and skin health support and 'beauty-from-within' nutricosmetics, plus rising Indian affluence and wellness spending.
- A multi-year structural gap in high-quality protein: severe whey protein supply shortages are pushing manufacturers toward collagen peptides not just as a substitute protein but as a functional ingredient improving texture, stability and consumer experience.
- A major further demand spike for collagen peptides is expected from GLP-1 medication, as healthcare providers commonly recommend high-protein intake to maintain muscle mass.
- Headwind: surplus supply of bovine hide gelatin and collagen peptides, as a weakening global leather industry pushes hide suppliers into gelatin/collagen, plus surplus Chinese capacity - this has weakened bone gelatin demand among low-quality-conscious customers, and closures of bone gelatin plants in the UK and US have released additional bone into the market.
- Margin lever from raw material: international crushed bone prices softened, enabling substantial Gelbone imports at higher yield/quality and reduced dependency on domestic bone, while hydrochloric acid and lime prices also decreased.
- Price/mix effects flagged: prices of Limed Ossein, Gelatin and Bovine Peptide fell 9%, 3% and 9% respectively while Ossein, Di-Calcium Phosphate and Fish Peptide rose 2%, 14% and 8%; collagen peptide volumes rose 57% but average realisation per unit fell 14.5% on mix change.
- DCP by-product realisation improved on better poultry-sector demand and on a new acid regulation making domestic Rock DCP production unviable alongside higher import costs.
- Government initiatives cited as supportive: 'Make in India', the pharma Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme, and Free Trade Agreements; India positioned as the 'Pharmacy of the World' and emerging as the 'Capital for nutraceutical/wellness products'.
- Watch items management flags for the year ahead: continuation or expansion of US tariff measures, geopolitical developments and regional conflicts, volatility in global trade flows, input price and availability, changes in government regulations and tax laws, and foreign exchange rate fluctuations.

risks.risk: US tariff exposure and trade-policy volatility
risks.note: Management states that with the imposition of US tariffs 'your product Gelatin became uncompetitive in the US market for a substantial period of time', forcing a deliberate reduction of US exposure and redirection of volumes; gelatin exports fell year on year as customers became 'wary about the risk of non-supply, if contracted'. The Chairman's message warns that the potential continuation or expansion of tariff measures by major economies, including the United States, warrants continued caution, and the cautionary statement lists tariffs imposed by the US administration as a factor that may affect operations.

risks.risk: Raw material cost and supply volatility, concentrated on a single input (crushed bone)
risks.note: Listed by management as 'Supply Chain Volatility: Fluctuating raw material costs, particularly in the bovine sector, can cause margin pressure.' Crushed bone is described as 'the major raw material of the Company'; FY26 benefited from softened international crushed bone prices and cheaper hydrochloric acid and lime, but the report also notes that 'certain factors have exerted significant pressure on bone gelatin costs'. Mitigation cited is investment in sustainable and traceable sourcing, long-term contracts and development of new cost-effective vendors.

'Pressure from substitutes: The growth of plant-based and synthetic (HPMC, Starch) capsules is challenging gelatin in specific, mostly premium or niche markets.' Demand for non-animal-based capsules such as HPMC and Pullulan is said to be increasing rapidly on dietary preferences. Management argues the shift is currently slowed by pharma-grade HPMC's high cost and 16-20-week lead times, and that gelatin remains dominant in the mainstream high-volume pharmaceutical segment - so the risk is structural but paced.

risks.risk: Competitive displacement by surplus hide-based gelatin and Chinese supply
risks.note: Surplus Chinese capacity and increased production of bovine hide gelatin and collagen peptides - driven by a weakening leather industry pushing hide suppliers into these outlets, and by closures of bone gelatin plants in the UK and US releasing additional bone - have created surplus supply and weakened bone gelatin demand among low-quality-conscious customers. Capsule makers are increasingly blending hide gelatin with bone gelatin to manage cost.

risks.risk: Deliberate market-share loss in the price-led segment
risks.note: 'The Company has taken a conscious call not to service Chinese Gelatin customers due to gap in quality expectation and pricing pressure, which has resulted in a decline in market share in this specific segment.' The strategy concentrates the business in brand-conscious and regulated segments, which held up in FY26 but narrows the addressable base if quality premiums compress.

Structural concentration disclosed in the Directors' Report: 'The entire sale of Ossein/Limed Ossein, 33% of the total sale of Gelatin and 69% of Collagen Peptide was through exports.' Ossein/limed ossein is entirely export-dependent and collagen peptide growth in FY26 leaned on a significant increase in North American demand - the same geography exposed to tariff action.

Prices of Limed Ossein, Gelatin and Bovine Peptide dropped by 9%, 3% and 9% respectively during 2025-26, and while collagen peptide volumes rose 57% the average realisation per unit declined 14.5% because of change in mix - volume growth is not translating one-for-one into value. Management notes price negotiations with both suppliers and customers are carried out on a regular basis to protect margins.

The cautionary statement enumerates that operations may be affected by the supply and demand situation, tariffs imposed by the US administration, input price and availability, changes in Government Regulations, Tax Laws and foreign exchange rate fluctuations. The report also shows regulation moving both ways for the Company - a new acid regulation made domestic Rock DCP production unviable, which lifted the Company's DCP realisation.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- The global capsule market including India is expanding steadily on rising pharmaceutical and nutraceutical reliance on capsules, with gelatin capsules expected to maintain a dominant 85% global market share.
- Near-term outlook for bone gelatin in both hard and soft capsule applications remains positive, supported by rising pharmaceutical production, increasing nutraceutical consumption and technological advances in capsule manufacturing.
- Bovine-derived bone gelatin retains a strong preferred position in pharmaceutical applications on consistent quality, high bloom strength and well-established safety standards, despite alternative materials emerging.
- Nutraceutical expansion is a key driver, with a projected 32% increase in demand for gelatin-based supplements; softgel applications are a 'high value-added segment' and hard gelatin capsules a 'structural demand pillar'.
- Substitution risk is contained near term: while HPMC is growing, its high cost and 16-20-week lead times for pharma-grade material restrict a rapid shift away from gelatin, preserving gelatin's market share in the mainstream high-volume pharmaceutical segment.
- Regional mix: Asia-Pacific is expected to be the fastest-growing region on expanding pharmaceutical manufacturing, while Europe continues to lead demand, particularly for premium and traceable gelatin.
- Collagen peptide demand is structurally supported by preventive healthcare, an ageing population seeking joint and skin health support and 'beauty-from-within' nutricosmetics, plus rising Indian affluence and wellness spending.
- A multi-year structural gap in high-quality protein: severe whey protein supply shortages are pushing manufacturers toward collagen peptides not just as a substitute protein but as a functional ingredient improving texture, stability and consumer experience.
- A major further demand spike for collagen peptides is expected from GLP-1 medication, as healthcare providers commonly recommend high-protein intake to maintain muscle mass.
- Headwind: surplus supply of bovine hide gelatin and collagen peptides, as a weakening global leather industry pushes hide suppliers into gelatin/collagen, plus surplus Chinese capacity - this has weakened bone gelatin demand among low-quality-conscious customers, and closures of bone gelatin plants in the UK and US have released additional bone into the market.
- Margin lever from raw material: international crushed bone prices softened, enabling substantial Gelbone imports at higher yield/quality and reduced dependency on domestic bone, while hydrochloric acid and lime prices also decreased.
- Price/mix effects flagged: prices of Limed Ossein, Gelatin and Bovine Peptide fell 9%, 3% and 9% respectively while Ossein, Di-Calcium Phosphate and Fish Peptide rose 2%, 14% and 8%; collagen peptide volumes rose 57% but average realisation per unit fell 14.5% on mix change.
- DCP by-product realisation improved on better poultry-sector demand and on a new acid regulation making domestic Rock DCP production unviable alongside higher import costs.
- Government initiatives cited as supportive: 'Make in India', the pharma Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme, and Free Trade Agreements; India positioned as the 'Pharmacy of the World' and emerging as the 'Capital for nutraceutical/wellness products'.
- Watch items management flags for the year ahead: continuation or expansion of US tariff measures, geopolitical developments and regional conflicts, volatility in global trade flows, input price and availability, changes in government regulations and tax laws, and foreign exchange rate fluctuations.

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Diversify markets and customer base to absorb US tariff disruption: exposure to the US market was deliberately reduced and gelatin volumes shifted to the domestic soft-capsule market and to emerging markets, with tariffs passed on to customers in several cases; the Company looks to bounce back in the US aided by an India-US Free Trade Agreement.
- Grow through capacity expansion in Gelatin and Collagen Peptides - listed explicitly as the 'Economic Sustainability' pillar alongside cost optimisation and supply chain efficiency.
- Compete on quality rather than price in gelatin: a conscious decision NOT to service Chinese-gelatin customers because of the gap in quality expectation and pricing pressure, accepting market-share loss in the low-quality-conscious segment while gaining share in brand-conscious / regulated segments.
- Secure and diversify raw material: invest in sustainable and traceable sourcing and long-term contracts, collaborate with industry participants to develop hide-based raw materials, import Gelbone when international crushed bone prices soften, and develop cost-effective new vendors and sources expected to aid profitability in the coming years.
- Widen the collagen peptide franchise by venturing into new markets and segments outside India, and build the consumer-facing Gelixer collagen nutrition brand (CollagenPep, Collagen Beauty, Collagen Active) positioned as India's first collagen brand.
- Sustained cost competitiveness and operational excellence: streamline operations, reduce costs and maximise output, run employee campaigns for innovative cost-reduction ideas, and hold plant utilisation at full/near-full capacity by rearranging customer and product mix.
- Energy and digital investment: install captive solar plants in two divisions (1.18 MW Gelatin Division, 0.78 MW Ossein Division) and complete the migration from SAP ECC to SAP S/4 HANA, with a proposed warehouse management module using bar coding and hand-held devices for real-time material tracking.
- Leverage the overseas promoter Nitta Gelatin Inc., Japan for technology, quality standards and market insight, and contribute to the Nitta Gelatin Group's Long-Term Management Vision announced in November 2025.
- Position products within a circular-economy / clean-label sustainability narrative: gelatin and collagen peptides are made from by-products of the meat and farmed fish industries, are natural proteins free from preservatives and additives, and sustainability considerations are embedded from product innovation and market development through to capital investments and daily operations.
- Organisation development: leadership continuity and succession (COO inducted, new CFO appointed with the incumbent moving to Chief Risk Officer), a three-tier L&D framework, values embedded into Level 1 leadership KRAs, the TEAM EXCITE engagement platform and an integrated HRMS.

themes.need: Rising protein/processed-food consumption, animal-nutrition demand and export tailwinds drive an integrated agri value-chain - DODLA/PARAGMILK on dairy; AVANTIFEED/SHINDL/SKMEGGPROD/HMAAGRO on aqua/poultry/meat protein; GODREJAGRO/KSCL/NATHBIOGEN on feed + seeds; REGAAL/SUKHJITS/GULPOLY on maize/starch; FOODSIN/MANORAMA on agri-processing & specialty fats.
themes.driver: Monsoon-led farm income; protein export demand; feed-margin recovery; festive processed-food restocking.

hero.oneLiner: Nitta Gelatin India Ltd. is a Kochi-based Indo-Japanese manufacturer of bone-derived gelatin, ossein and collagen peptides for the pharmaceutical and nutraceutical industries, exporting 69% of its collagen peptide output.
